open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform deterministic excess-risk separation for the cross-fitted common-versus-piecewise affine profile, and its conversion into a cutoff tail with fully evaluated constants.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact Gram lower bound controls coefficient stability, and the stopped Bernstein calculation controls a fixed sequential process, but the profiled quadratic score contains fitted common and piecewise coefficients.  A uniform comparison of those random fitted scores to one population profile, with no cross-side derivative matching, is still needed before the sequential bound can be applied.  Consequently the formerly asserted constants \(2^{-28}\) and \(2^{-30}\) are not justified.
open_obligations.attempted: The unit-flank Gram was recomputed exactly as \(H(4-\sqrt{13})/6\), the half-eigenvalue fallback was made explicit, \(H\) was retained, \(\delta\) was changed everywhere to \(\kappa_n/32\), and the exponential-series argument was carried through to the stopped sequential Bernstein formula.  Substitution into the desired profile inequalities was stopped where the missing population-to-empirical profile comparison is required.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper studies fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when both the compliance jump and its unknown cutoff become statistically weak.  The finite-sample location-mixture converse proves a nonshrinking barrier below the signal-to-entropy boundary.  At \(s=1\), a total four-fold rectangular scan--refine--invert rule attains the known-cutoff order when \(n\kappa_n^3\) dominates \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\).  For \(s>1\), an explicit affine-profile map and fallback are defined, but the same-class bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) remains an open question because its profile maximal inequality and matching slope-kink lower pair are not yet proved.  The fixed-level critical-window law also remains open.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak fuzzy-RD inference and fixed-jump unknown-cutoff localization do not characterize honest connected LATE-interval length when the first-stage denominator and its location weaken jointly; in particular, neither supplies the higher-smoothness cutoff-uncertainty term under separate one-sided smoothness.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment combines a nonconvex union over cutoff locations, a causal outcome--treatment ratio, separate one-sided smoothness that permits a derivative kink, and fixed-level connected-length loss.  Its critical and higher-smoothness detectable regions cannot be inferred from a point-estimation cutoff rate.
project_justification.fill: The project fixes one observable-law class, proves the finite-sample location-mixture converse, and gives a total four-fold interval attaining known-cutoff order on the Lipschitz face.  For \(s>1\), it now exposes a measurable common-versus-piecewise affine profile with an explicit fallback and isolates the unresolved bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) without strengthening the class or claiming unproved constants.

prose_updates.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) motivate the observable class and known-cutoff bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion for weak fuzzy-RD designs.  Porter and Yu (2015) obtain unknown-cutoff oracle substitution under a fixed discontinuity in a sharp-design treatment-effect problem.  Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) motivate multiscale scan architecture, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) provide general maximal-control tools; neither supplies the present uniform causal connected-length theorem.  M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) and Tuvaandorj (2020) concern shrinking-jump or nonparametric location experiments, and no equation-level proposition from Tuvaandorj is used here.  Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) supply an ordered-modulus and test-inversion template for convex fixed-index classes.  Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) study aligned multivariate change channels without the monotone fuzzy-RD causal restrictions.  Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) use a Bayesian unknown-cutoff fuzzy-RD model, and Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) discuss fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately.  The proved frontier advance here consists of the finite-sample converse and the Lipschitz oracle-attainment theorem.  The higher-smoothness bracket and the exact critical-window connected-length law remain explicit open questions.
prose_updates.interpretation: At \(s=1\), the localization index \(n\kappa_n^3\) pays the logarithmic search cost, after which an independent fixed-center inversion has length \(n^{-1/3}/\kappa_n\), exactly the known-cutoff order.  For \(s>1\), separate affine profiling is designed to absorb an unrestricted derivative kink.  If it localizes at order \(1/(n\kappa_n^2)\), the kink contributes \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) after division by the compliance jump; proving that localization and a matching lower pair is the remaining detectable-region problem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-smoothness profile branch is a total measurable estimator, not a proved performance theorem.  Its unit-flank population Gram has exact minimum eigenvalue \(H(4-\sqrt{13})/6\), its fallback uses half that value, and the approximation tolerance is \(\delta=\kappa_n/32\).  The stopped Bernstein inequality is derived, but the uniform population-to-empirical comparison for the quadratic profile has not been closed, so the previously suggested \(2^{-28}\) and \(2^{-30}\) constants are not asserted.  A same-class slope-kink converse for \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) and the sharp critical-window law also remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, known-cutoff benchmark, and finite-sample location-mixture barrier retain their full stated scope.  Oracle-order attainment is proved only on the Lipschitz face \(s=1\), uniformly over vanishing \(\kappa_n\) satisfying the displayed signal condition.  For \(s>1\), the paper defines the profile-based rule and poses, but does not claim, the detectable-region bracket.  No cross-side derivative matching, latent-cell H{\"o}lder restriction, adaptation guarantee, disconnected-set result, or matched critical-window constant is added.
